title: Request needleboard — compact synthesis and rapid patches
summary: Short distillation of customer asks from Apr customer calls + support threads (n≈18). Focus: small-surface fixes that unblock production usage vs larger product bets. This is intentionally compact — needleboard = pin the smallest high-impact asks together for fast engineering sprints.
signal_clusters: Latency/variability in single-turn generation (hosted API) — customers report periodic 300–700ms spikes on 1k token requests; most sensitive are chat UIs and autocomplete flows.
Model fallback opacity — users want clearer signals when the platform routes to a quantized or smaller variant during capacity constraints.
Billing surprises — token rounding and unexpected micro-charges from prefix deduping/caching leading to billing disputes.
Dev ergonomics — lack of per-request metadata tagging and difficulty correlating logs to customer traces (esp. for private deployments).
Embedding consistency — small numeric drift between model versions breaking vector-store similarity thresholds for recommender systems.
representative_quotes: "We saw a sudden 50% drop in top-2 click rate on suggestions during a 1-hour window — nothing in our stack changed." — fintech app PM
"Why did my call get rerouted? The quality went down and the user noticed. We need a flag in the response." — ecommerce search engineer
"Our billing batch shows 0.02 token units difference across two identical requests. Customers are asking for an explanation." — head of integrations
priority_requests: Add per-response routing metadata (model_variant, quantized=true/false, region, fallback_reason) — low effort, high trust payoff.
Expose a lightweight latency histogram endpoint per API key (p95/p99 over last 24h) — helps SREs and customers avoid blaming their infra.
Introduce a "quiet-billing" diagnostic mode (show raw token accounting + cache hits) for partners disputing invoices — gated behind support.
Embedding-sanity check endpoint to surface version-drift stats for a small sample set — quick integration helper for customers upgrading models.
Per-request tags/metadata passthrough so customers can map tokens/calls to their tracing IDs in Console logs.
quick_fixes_proposals: Server-side: attach routing metadata to existing response headers (no schema change to payload) — engineer estimate: 2 dev days + 1 QA day.
Console: add API-key latency panel showing rolling p95/p99 and recent anomalies — PM/UX quick wire needed; backend mostly re-use metrics.
Billing: add a support-only debug export for token accounting (CSV) that explains rounding and cache deductions — support+billing owning triage flow.
Docs: publish a 'Model fallback behavior' short note with examples of when and how fallbacks happen and how to pin versions — 1 writer day.
Embeddings: 'canary compare' script in SDK that computes small-dataset drift between two model versions and surfaces a short summary — SDK + examples, 3 dev days.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Adding per-response routing metadata could increase response size and slightly affect latency; mitigate by putting into headers and adding opt-out flag.
Exposing detailed billing diagnostics may create more support tickets and legal questions; gate via support request and rate-limit the export.
Embedding drift tooling may encourage lock-in if customers rely solely on our internal drift metric; provide clear guidance and encourage local validation.

Ethan: prototype adding 'x-redwood-variant' header on a test endpoint and run a 48h smoke with traffic replay — estimate 5 days.
Samir: draft 'billing debug export' RFC and ownership flow for support > billing teams — deliver by 2026-04-27.
Marta: quick UX sketch for API-key latency panel and upload to Confluence — due 2026-04-23.
Docs owner (TBD): write fallback behavior note and pin to 'status' section in docs — target 2026-04-30.
open_questions: Should routing metadata be opt-in per customer or on by default? (privacy + payload size considerations).
What SLAs (if any) apply to the new latency histogram endpoint? Who owns alerting?
How to gate the billing debug export to avoid adversarial usage — token-based access, support approvals, or signed agreement?
notes_to_self: This is a compact instrument for our next 'rapid patch' sprint. Keep scope small: focus on observable signals customers can consume without heavy platform changes. Iterate quickly and surface early prototypes to 2 customers for feedback.
